title: Chapter 111: Getting Closer
html:
Chen Ge and Doctor Gao fell silent. Washing one’s hair symbolized cleansing away dirt and misfortune; in traditional dream interpretation, it foretold good things. Nothing about Men Nan’s experience sounded fortunate. It was a nightmare.

“Can you still remember the face of the person in your dream and your surroundings?”

Men Nan was probably the black phone’s special visitor, which meant Chen Ge’s choices could determine the final reward.

“It seems to happen in the bathroom of my apartment. The layout feels familiar, but I can’t be certain.” Men Nan bowed his head farther, his voice weakening. “I’ve never seen the person beside me clearly, but I know he’s getting closer. I have the same dream every night, and each time the room becomes sharper. So does his face.”

“What does he look like?”

“Next time, I’ll see his face.” Men Nan kept his head bowed and looked up with only his eyes, giving him a disturbing appearance. His answer remained frustratingly vague.

Chen Ge pressed on. “Tell me everything you remember. What did the man do while you washed your hair? Did he ever speak?”

“The dream is almost always the same.” Men Nan’s raw voice trembled. “When it began three weeks ago, it wasn’t so frightening. I would wake in the middle of the night and enter the bathroom. My mind was empty, and my body moved by itself, as though something else controlled me.

“At first everything was blurred. I stood before the mirror, filled a basin, and lowered my head into the water. Bent over like that, I could see an upside-down figure standing at the apartment’s front door.

“He was far away. Only after I finished washing did I realize he had moved a little closer.

“Other dreams followed, so I paid it little attention. But the next night, it happened again.

“Everything repeated. I entered the bathroom, stood before the mirror, filled the basin, and lowered my head. The moment my hair touched the water, I saw someone in the living room. When I finished, he was closer again.

“The dream returned night after night. At first it felt ordinary, but every repetition became more vivid. I could think and feel everything—and the man moved closer each time.

“I’m terrified, but I can’t wake up. Whenever I sleep, the dream continues. Two and a half weeks ago, he entered the living room. A week ago, he reached the bathroom. Four days ago, he stood beside me.

“When I bent toward the water, he leaned with me, his blurred face inching closer to mine.”

The description alone chilled Chen Ge. He could barely imagine enduring it firsthand. Three weeks of the same nightmare, with an unknown man creeping closer each night, would break almost anyone.

“The night before last, I dreamed it again. That was the last time.” Men Nan tried to raise his head, his eyes darting wildly. “His face was close enough to see. Then his hands closed around my throat. I woke up, and I haven’t slept since.”

Men Nan’s situation was desperate. The figure had begun strangling him, and no one knew what the next dream would bring. No wonder Doctor Gao had turned to Chen Ge as a last resort.

“A recurring dream, always in the bathroom…” Chen Ge considered it. “Could the apartment itself be the problem? This is only a possibility, so don’t panic.”

“Go on.”

“Could someone have died in your apartment without the body being discovered? Perhaps the victim is entering your dreams so you’ll call the police.”

Men Nan’s face turned ashen. He dragged in a deep breath. “A body in my apartment? Impossible!”

His emotions began spiraling. Without Doctor Gao’s hands steadying his shoulders, he might have become violent. “I’ve inspected his apartment thoroughly and found nothing unusual,” the doctor said. “A week ago, I invited Men Nan to stay with me. The change of location did not stop the dream.”

“In the first dream, the man stood outside the front door, so he may have come from elsewhere in the building. We shouldn’t limit the search to Men Nan’s apartment.” Chen Ge kept the rest of his theory to himself. The ghost had probably attached itself to Men Nan, which would explain why sleeping elsewhere accomplished nothing.

“We aren’t police; we have no authority to search the building.” Doctor Gao seemed to regret consulting him. “We should analyze the dream. Men Nan repeatedly washes his hair. Understanding that action may reveal the source.”

Chen Ge listened patiently, but the psychological interpretation could not explain why the identical dream returned every night.

“I can’t be certain yet. Let’s visit Men Nan’s apartment tonight. A new pair of eyes may notice something you missed.” Chen Ge waited for their answer with his hands in his pockets. Since the special-visitor alert, the black phone had offered no further guidance.
